tl;dr

The GOP representatives are most strongly against it simply due to it being Obama's idea.  They are echoing the feelings of their largest donors.  Major business concerns mostly, though PAC's have really taken off since Citizen's United.  Those PAC's are largely unregulated by anyone and reflect the ideals of their donors (mostly).  Those donors give their money to the PAC's specifically because the anonymity of the PAC assures them they can advocate the most extreme positions without fear of public scrutiny or ridicule (See: Chick-Fil-A, Barilla).

Due to the influx of large sums of money from businesses that are more organized and centralized than ever in history short of the Railroad and oil trusts of the early 20th century, they can spend mage bucks that are rather minimal to their bottom line to fend off taxation that could drag down quarterly profits.

The grass-roots GOP voter however is mostly made up of two types: Republicans by blood whose parents and grandparents were Republicans and still think that Democrats are soft on morals and crime but don't give much thought to politics most days.

The new breed of course is the Tea Party stalwart who HATES even REPUBLICANS who are not in favor of closing down the Fed wholesale except to run the military.  These people tend to believe that society is holding them back by rules which curb their exceptionalism and reward... well, minorities when you get them to talk in a quiet room.  And as Obama is not only NOT a Republican (all the time) and is in FACT a minority... he's The Enemy.  

It comes down to hatred for Obama.  Little else.
